newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha jumps with crude, combats freight rate.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha jumps with crude, combats freight rate.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices charged higher on Thursday after sharp gains in crude oil the last two days and as high freight rates forced a closer look at co-loading cargoes, traders said.
Feb swaps rose about $1.50 to $224.25/$225.50 a tonne and March gained the same to $218.75/$219.75, after Brent crude soared 52 cents on Wednesday and added another five cents today.

"There is still good demand for the high paraffinic, and for the heavy naphtha there is not, due to the poor refining margins," a trader said, adding naphtha continue to march higher as long as crude extends its gains.
He said a cargo of light paraffinic was sold today in NWE at cif high quotes +$3.25, but no other details were available.
Cargoes were notionally assessed at $226/$228 cif for NWE. Med cargoes traded at $223/$225 cif, with fob prices holding at a very wide discount at $207/$209 due to the high freight rates.
A fob cargo was confirmed sold by a Spanish end-user on a private and confidential basis earlier this week in the Med.
Traders speculated the cargo was being sent to the U.S. after Nova, according to shipping sources, fixed a 57,000 tonne cargo from Skikda to the U.S. Gulf Coast for early February.
Mira also fixed a 55,000 tonne vessel out of Skikda with options for Northwest Europe and the U.S. for mid-February, the shipping sources said.
One trader said there was speculation that another 60,000 tonne Skikda cargo was heading for Tarragona, Spain, for mid-February. This could not be confirmed.
But this trader said he believed some end-users were covered for most of February for Northwest Europe. He added the arbitrage was shut to the U.S. for fixed price material.
